hero: Inside a bright adult hemodialysis unit in Central Luzon, a twelve-year-old Filipino boy sits in a large dialysis chair that looks too big for him, a tunneled catheter dressing visible below his right collarbone. A female pediatric nephrologist in a white coat kneels at eye level, gently inspecting the dressing while a dialysis nurse in scrubs holds the chart; his mother sits close, holding his hand. Adult patients rest in the background chairs. Warm morning light, calm and attentive mood, no text.

figures.teaches: Which veins to protect from birth in a child with CKD and why central narrowing is silent.
figures.content: Front-view outline of a school-age child. Green-highlighted: forearm veins and upper-arm veins on both arms labeled 'Future fistula'. Blue-highlighted: right internal jugular vein labeled 'Catheter route'. Red X over left arm PICC path labeled 'No PICC' and over subclavian vein labeled 'Avoid subclavian'. Small inset of a narrowed central vein labeled 'Silent stenosis'. Footer label: 'Every vein is the next access'.

figures.teaches: How to link a catheter alarm to its likely cause and the right moment to call.
figures.content: Four rows, each with an icon: 1) 'Inflow alarm, positional' -> 'Tip position' -> 'Chest film if recurs'. 2) 'Cannot aspirate' -> 'Thrombus' -> 'Call same session'. 3) 'Venous pressure rising' -> 'Clotting or kink' -> 'Check circuit'. 4) 'Neck or arm swelling' -> 'Central vein thrombosis' -> 'Call now'. Header split: 'Early = position' and 'Late = clot or sheath'.

figures.teaches: The first 30 minutes and the removal decision for fever during HD through a catheter.
figures.content: Start box 'Rigors after connection'. Arrow to 'Stop fluid removal, vital signs'. Arrow to 'Cultures before antibiotics'. Arrow to 'First dose within the hour'. Arrow to 'Call attending'. Branch 'Unstable?' yes -> 'Transfer today'. Decision box 'Organism?': 'S. aureus, Pseudomonas, Candida' -> 'Remove catheter'; 'Other organism' -> 'Better in 2 to 3 days?' yes -> 'Lock or guidewire exchange'; no -> 'Remove catheter'.

card: A child's arm resting on a dialysis chair armrest with a soft bandage at the wrist and a gentle hand of a clinician beside it, warm light, no text.
